summary: Owned units s0001–s0022 were read in Chinese for omitted births, deaths, ages, and date context. The only explicit age is Wang Xizhi's 年十三, kept as sui and not turned into a birth year. The only death in these units is Yu Liang's 亮臨薨, identified as Chengdi Xiankang 6 / AD 340 from the Jinshu annals and biography; the first-month death remains Western 340 on a Gregorian reading and is Yu Liang's own event, while Xizhi's mention in that memorial is living attestation rather than retrospective reception. Yuan Di's 過江 and Wang Kuang's proposal convert to AD 307 from 永嘉初 plus Tongjian Yongjia 1 month 9, a reign-year label, not a pretended Gregorian day. One-sided bounds onOrBefore 322 (Zhou Yi killed in Yongchang 1), 324 (Wang Dun died Taining 2), 339 (Xi Jian died Xiankang 5), and 353 (Yin Hao beaten by Yao Xiang in Yonghe 9) date the named persons' own meetings, speech, clerkship, marriage, and letters; they do not fill dynasties or feed later honors into life dates. Yu Liang's Zhengxi recruitment sits in the 334–340 uncertainty window opened by 進號征西 after Tao Kan's death and closed by Yu Liang's death. Undated offices and the 三少 naming were left unresolved. Hints match these supported personal events. No chronology finding remains.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi is stated to have been thirteen sui when he called on Zhou Yi.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Wang Xizhi. Unit s0007 says 年十三 of Xizhi himself; this is an age claim, not a birth year. The extraction keeps reckoning sui and does not convert inclusive age into a Western birth year. No competing age figure appears in the owned units.

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang died after composing a deathbed memorial that praised Wang Xizhi.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Yu Liang. 亮臨薨 is Yu Liang's own approaching death, not a later commemoration. Jinshu Cheng Di annals date the death to 咸康六年春正月庚子 under Chengdi of Eastern Jin; Yu Liang's biography repeats 咸康六年薨. That reign year is the conventional AD 340 label. The memorial falls in the first Chinese month, which DILA's Gregorian setting places at 340-02-15, so the Western year does not slip to 339. Year precision is correct: the chapter has no month/day, and a reign-year label is not treated as a Gregorian calendar day.

evidence.quote: 亮臨薨，上疏稱羲之清貴有鑒裁。

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi at thirteen sui visited Zhou Yi and was first offered the ox-heart roast.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Wang Xizhi. The visit is his own event; Zhou Yi had to be alive to receive him. Jinshu records Zhou Yi's killing during Wang Dun's Yongchang 1 attack on Jiankang (敦收周顗、戴若思害之), and Yuan Di's annals open that rising in 永昌元年正月. Yongchang 1 is the AD 322 reign-year label. onOrBefore 322 is the right one-sided bound: the call can still fall in 322 before the killing. The source date remains 年十三; no birth year is inferred from sui.

evidence.quote: 年十三，嘗謁周顗，顗察而異之。
顗先割啖羲之，於是始知名。

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi in childhood was slow of speech and not thought remarkable.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Wang Xizhi. 幼 marks childhood only. No reign year, month, or Western date is present, and the claim correctly stays undated rather than guessing a year from later career dates.

evidence.quote: 羲之幼訥於言，人未之奇。

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi in adulthood was eloquent, famed for integrity, and preeminent in clerical script.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Wang Xizhi. 及長 is a life-stage note, not a dated office or campaign. Leaving the attestation undated avoids turning a general characterization into a false activity year.

evidence.quote: 及長，辯贍，以骨鯁稱，尤善隸書

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi was commended for integrity and judgment in Yu Liang's deathbed memorial.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Wang Xizhi. The memorial names him while Yu Liang is dying, so this is living attestation, not retrospective reception. The date is Yu Liang's death year, Eastern Jin Chengdi 咸康六年, conventional AD 340. DILA's proleptic Gregorian range for that death begins 340-02-15, confirming the Western year. The chapter sequence then promotes Xizhi (s0021), which is consistent with a living honor in 340.

evidence.quote: 亮臨薨，上疏稱羲之清貴有鑒裁。

itemChecks.event: Wang Dao is identified as Minister of Education only in Wang Xizhi's kinship line.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Wang Dao. 司徒導 is a genealogical title with no reign year in s0002. Treating it as an undated attestation is required; the later 王丞相時 window belongs to a different unit and must not be read back into this kinship sentence.

itemChecks.event: Wang Zheng is attested as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing with no reign year.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Wang Zheng. s0003 gives only 尚書郎. No birth, death, age, or reign date appears, so an undated attestation is the complete chronology the unit supports.

itemChecks.event: Wang Kuang first proposed the plan when Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Wang Kuang. 曠首創其議 is his own counsel, tied by the narrator to 元帝之過江也. Jinshu Yuan Di annals say 永嘉初，用王导计，始镇建邺; Tongjian specifies 永嘉元年九月戊申 arrival at Jianye and labels that year 西元三〇七年. 永嘉初 is a looser phrasing of the same opening of Yongjia, not a competing later year. September of Yongjia 1 remains AD 307 and is not a New Year boundary case. Year precision matches a reign-year identification of the crossing; the chapter itself has no month/day.

evidence.quote: 元帝之過江也，曠首創其議。

itemChecks.event: Wang Kuang is named Administrator of Huainan in the genealogy without a reign year.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Wang Kuang. 淮南太守 is an undated office label in the opening pedigree. It must stay unresolved as to year; the 307 crossing is a different event and does not date this title.

itemChecks.event: Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi and established himself at Jianye.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Emperor Yuan (Sima Rui). 元帝之過江也 is his own southward crossing, later so called; in Yongjia 1 he was still Langye Prince. Primary witnesses are Jinshu 永嘉初始鎮建鄴 and Tongjian 永嘉元年九月戊申至建業, AD 307. The event is the crossing, not the 317 princely or 318 imperial accession. Year 307 is the reign-year label for Yongjia 1, not a converted month/day Gregorian calendar date.

itemChecks.event: Zhou Yi received the thirteen-sui Wang Xizhi and first offered him the ox-heart roast.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Zhou Yi. Receiving the boy and serving the roast are his own acts. He was killed in Wang Dun's Yongchang 1 occupation of Jiankang, so the meeting is on or before AD 322, the Yongchang 1 label. The bound is Zhou Yi's death year, not a claim that the visit fills the whole year. No second endpoint is invented.

evidence.quote: 年十三，嘗謁周顗，顗察而異之。

itemChecks.event: Wang Dun as paternal uncle esteemed Wang Xizhi and compared him with Clerk Ruan.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Wang Dun. 敦嘗謂羲之 is Dun's own speech while he is alive. Ming Di annals record 王敦憤惋而死 in 太寧二年秋七月; that reign year is AD 324. onOrBefore 324 is the inclusive death bound. The source phrase 從伯敦 is not itself a year, and the conversion is contextual, which the certainty label already marks.

itemChecks.event: Ruan Yu served as Wang Dun's chief clerk and was named by Dun as the standard for Xizhi.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Ruan Yu. 為敦主簿 is his service under Dun, which cannot postdate Dun's death in Taining 2 / AD 324. onOrBefore 324 is a one-sided bound on that clerkship, not a claim that Ruan Yu's whole career ends in 324.

evidence.quote: 時陳留阮裕有重名，為敦主簿。

itemChecks.event: Ruan Yu grouped Wang Cheng with Xizhi and Wang Yue as the three young men of the Wang clan.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Wang Cheng. He is only named in the 王氏三少 remark. No reign year or age is given, and 同生 is not used. Leaving the attestation undated is required; Dun's death bound must not be copied onto Cheng.

evidence.quote: 裕亦目羲之與王承、王悅為王氏三少。

itemChecks.event: Ruan Yu grouped Wang Yue with Xizhi and Wang Cheng as the three young men of the Wang clan.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Wang Yue. The same undated 三少 notice names him. No year is inferable from the maternal or clan list, and the claim correctly stays undated.

evidence.quote: 羲之與王承、王悅為王氏三少。

itemChecks.event: Xi Jian, then titled Grand Commandant, sent a student to Wang Dao to seek a son-in-law.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Xi Jian. Seeking the son-in-law is his act. Cheng Di annals record 太尉、南昌公郗鑒薨 in 咸康五年八月; that death year is AD 339. onOrBefore 339 is the safe one-sided bound. 時太尉 may be contemporaneous or an anachronistic highest title (he became Taiwei only in 咸康四年五月 / AD 338), so inventing an 338 start would create false precision against the narrative order that places the match before Xizhi's first office. The extraction keeps only the death bound.

itemChecks.event: Xi Jian's daughter was given in marriage to Wang Xizhi after the east-wing inspection.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Xi Jian's daughter. 遂以女妻之 is her marriage, which cannot fall after her father's death in Xiankang 5 / AD 339. onOrBefore 339 dates that marriage as a one-sided bound and does not turn 太尉 tenure into an exact wedding year.

evidence.quote: 訪之，乃羲之也，遂以女妻之。

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang, as General Who Conquers the West, requested Wang Xizhi as an army adviser.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Yu Liang. 征西將軍庾亮請為參軍 is his recruitment of Xizhi, a point event during the Zhengxi tenure, not activity smeared across a dynasty. The biography says that on Tao Kan's death Yu Liang 進號征西將軍; Cheng Di annals place Tao Kan's death in 咸和九年六月 (AD 334). Yu Liang then dies 咸康六年正月 (AD 340). The 334–340 interval is therefore the uncertainty window for the request, with both endpoints justified by Yu Liang's own title change and death.

evidence.quote: 征西將軍庾亮請為參軍，累遷長史。

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang, near death, submitted a memorial praising Wang Xizhi.
itemChecks.reason: The owner is Yu Liang. 亮臨薨 is the same death-year event as claim-115. Chengdi 咸康六年 / AD 340 is the reign-year label, and the first-month death stays in Western 340 under a Gregorian reading. This is a deathbed act, not later reception of Yu Liang.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi was commended in Yu Liang's deathbed memorial and later wrote to restrain Yin Hao before Yao Xiang's victory.
itemChecks.reason: The listed hints match supported living events, not posthumous reception. AD 340 is the deathbed commendation in s0020. on or before AD 353 follows the context letters before Yin Hao's northern defeat: Tongjian dates that campaign to 永和九年冬十月 and labels the year 公元三五三年. onOrBefore 353 is inclusive of the defeat year and does not invent a start year. The earlier Zhou Yi visit (on or before 322) is a separate owned claim and does not contradict these later activity hints.

Formal 丞相 lasts only 咸康四年–五年, but 王丞相 is the conventional epithet for that ministerial span. Owned s0002 remains an undated 司徒 label and is not overwritten.

personChecks.reason: Owned units give Wang Xizhi an explicit sui age (年十三) and no birth or death. The childhood visit is his own event on or before Zhou Yi's Yongchang 1 death (AD 322). Adulthood praise in s0009 is undated. Yu Liang's 臨薨 memorial in 咸康六年 (AD 340) attests living commendation, after which s0021 promotes him; that is not retrospective reception and must not be discarded. Context letters to Yin Hao sit before the 永和九年 / AD 353 Yao Xiang defeat, so on or before 353 is a valid later activity bound. Hints list 340 and on or before 353, which match those supported living events and do not convert sui into a birth year. Endpoints are Jianwu 1 / AD 317 (Yuan Di as Jin Prince; Dao already the chief minister) and Dao's own death in 咸康五年 / AD 339. That interval is uncertainty about one recruitment, not a dynasty-filling activity bar. No birth, death, or age is stated in the owned units themselves.
Wang Zheng appears only as 尚書郎 in the grandfather slot. Owned units omit birth, death, age, and any reign year; empty hints match that silence.

Two distinct Wang Kuang facts are kept apart: undated 淮南太守, and the Yongjia 1 crossing proposal dated AD 307 as Kuang's own counsel. No age or death is given. The 307 year belongs to the crossing-plan event, not to the Huainan title.

Emperor Yuan's only owned dated event is the Yangzi crossing. Jinshu's 永嘉初 and Tongjian's 永嘉元年九月戊申 both identify the move that opens Yongjia, AD 307. Later imperial accession years are not substituted for this event, and no death or age is extracted from these units.

Zhou Yi's only owned event is receiving the thirteen-sui Xizhi. The latest possible year is Zhou Yi's own killing in Yongchang 1 / AD 322. No birth or sui age for Zhou Yi is stated here, and later gifts or slander after death are not used.
Wang Dun's owned acts are esteeming Xizhi and speaking the Ruan comparison. Both require Dun alive, hence on or before Taining 2 / AD 324. No birth or age appears in the owned units.

Ruan Yu is Dun's 主簿 and the speaker of the 三少 remark. Only the clerkship is given a death-bound of AD 324; the 三少 notice stays undated. That split preserves sequence without inventing years for the naming.
